t:
(a) Limitation.—Of the amounts authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2009 by section 3101(a)(2) for defense nuclear nonproliferation activities, not more than $3,000,000 may be used for projects that are specifically designed for the Global Nuclear Energy Partnership. Any amount so used may not be expended until 30 days after the date on which the Administrator of the National Nuclear Security Administration submits to Congress a report that describes in detail the full amount of funding that the Administrator plans to expend for any effort related to the Global Nuclear Energy Partnership. 
    (b) Use of Funds.—Any amount made available pursuant to an authorization of appropriations under section 3101(a)(2) that is covered by the limitation under subsection (a) shall only be available for nonproliferation risk assessments relating to the Global Nuclear Energy Partnership and related work on export control reviews and determinations.

fable.w: The section caps funding for Global Nuclear Energy Partnership projects and conditions spending on a report to Congress, which is inside the federal government. The tempting reading is that the report requirement or the word "Partnership" signals outside involvement, but the report stays within the government and "Partnership" is only a proper noun. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, and no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: may not be expended until 30 days after the date on which the Administrator of the National Nuclear Security Administration submits to Congress a report

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Administrator to submit a report to Congress before expending funds. Congress is part of the federal government, so this interaction is internal to the government and does not involve outside parties. The 30-day delay is a procedural constraint on spending, not a mechanism for public participation or consultation with non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: Any amount so used may not be expended until 30 days after the date on which the Administrator of the National Nuclear Security Administration submits to Congress a report that describes in detail the full amount of funding that the Administrator plans to expend for any effort related to the Global Nuclear Energy Partnership.

opus.w: The only procedural step here is a report from a federal official (the Administrator) to Congress. Both are inside the federal government, so the report does not bring in anyone from outside. The word "Partnership" is part of a program name and does not create any process involving outside parties. The rest of the section only caps funding and limits what it can be used for.
opus.s: Any amount so used may not be expended until 30 days after the date on which the Administrator of the National Nuclear Security Administration submits to Congress a report that describes in detail the full amount of funding that the Administrator plans to expend for any effort related to the Global Nuclear Energy Partnership.
opus.b:
**Step 1: The tempting reading.** The section sounds procedural. It delays spending until a report goes to Congress, and it names a "Partnership." But Congress is inside the federal government, so a report to Congress is not participation. "Global Nuclear Energy Partnership" is just the name of a program. The section never requires the government to consult states, experts, companies or the public, or to hold hearings, take comments or issue rules. It only limits and directs how appropriated money is used.

**Step 2: Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Administrator of the National Nuclear Security Administration to submit a report to Congress before expending certain funds. According to the definition, Congress is inside the federal government, and reports to Congress are explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. There is no consultation or coordination with any outside party (such as states, tribes, or the public) involved in this decision.
qwen_chat.s: Any amount so used may not be expended until 30 days after the date on which the Administrator of the National Nuclear Security Administration submits to Congress a report that describes in detail the full amount of funding that the Administrator plans to expend for any effort related to the Global Nuclear Energy Partnership.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement to submit a report to Congress constitutes "participation" because it involves a procedural step before funds can be used. However, the definition explicitly states that reports to Congress are "inside the federal government" and thus do not count as participation. The only interaction described is between a federal agency (NNSA) and Congress, with no involvement of outside parties (states, tribes, public, etc.) in the decision-making process.
